title: Signals Intelligence/Electromagnetic Warfare Chief (MGySgt to MSgt) PMOS, DIR INTEL
raw_text:
12. MOS 2691, Signals Intelligence/Electromagnetic Warfare Chief (MGySgt to
MSgt) PMOS, DIR INTEL

    a. Summary. Duties encompass signals intelligence (SIGINT),
electromagnetic warfare (EW), planning, personnel and asset management,
collection management, analysis, dissemination efforts, and ensuring
national-to-tactical SIGINT/EW integration. SIGINT/EW Chiefs also supervise
the activities of personnel performing communications intercept, electronic
reconnaissance, radio direction finding, analysis and reporting functions,
intelligence support to CO, and EW operations. They may also be assigned to
the intelligence staff marine corps forces special operations command
(MARSOC), marine cryptologic support battalion (MCSB), radio battalions,
marine littoral regiments (MLR), and the staff sections of the MEF
information groups (MIG), marine divisions (MARDIV), marine corps forces
commands, and marine aviation wings (MAW) supervising special security and
special intelligence support functions. Additionally, they serve in staff
billets as operational advisors designated by the commander or cognizant
staff officer.

       b.   Prerequisites

            (1) Must hold MOS 2629.

            (2) Must be a U.S. citizen.

        (3) Must successfully complete a counter-intelligence scope polygraph
examination.

        (4) Security requirement: must have a current single scope
background investigation/TS investigation and adjudicated for sensitive
compartmented information (SCI) eligibility.

       c.   Requirements.   MOS granted upon promotion to master sergeant.



                                          3-167                       Enclosure (1)
 3122                                                           NAVMC 1200.1L



    d. Duties. For a complete listing of duties and tasks, refer to
reference (p), Signals Intelligence Training and Readiness Manual.

    e. Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code.
First-Line Supervisors/Managers of All Other Tactical Operations Specialists
55-2013.

       f.   Related Military Skill

            (1) COMINT/EW Operator, 2621.

            (2) SIGINT/EW Technician, 2629.

            (3) SIGINT/EW Analyst, 2631.

            (4) Cryptologic Language Analyst, 2641.




                                           3-168                 Enclosure (1)
 3123                                                                 NAVMC 1200.1L

The Signals Intelligence (SIGINT), Electromagnetic Warfare (EW) OccFld includes the employment of SIGINT, EW, support to cyberspace operations (CO) and intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance (ISR) systems engineering capabilities. Marines in this field are required to set up and operate collection and communications electronic equipment, manage intelligence data, prepare EW and intelligence reports, extend and mesh intelligence services, conduct preventive maintenance on assigned equipment, execute electromagnetic attack (EA), and assist in the operational control and management of SIGINT/EW/CO personnel, equipment, and facilities. Entry- level jobs include Communications Intelligence/Electromagnetic Warfare Operator, Signals Intelligence/Electromagnetic Warfare Analyst, Intelligence Surveillance Reconnaissance Systems Engineer, and Cryptologic Language Analyst. Marines can LATMOV into the 2600 OccFld at the grade of corporal or sergeant. Sergeants requesting LATMOV into the 2600 OccFld must have no more than 1 year time in grade. Duty assignments include Marine Forces Special Operations Command (MARSOC), Marine Corps Information Command (MCIC), Marine Forces Cyber Command (MARFORCYBER), Marine Cryptologic Support Battalion (MCSB), radio battalions, intelligence battalions, infantry battalions, littoral combat team (LCT), marine littoral regiments (MLR), and the staff sections of the MEF information groups (MIG), Marine divisions (MARDIV), and Marine aviation wings (MAW).

Marines in this field are required to set up and operate collection and communications electronic equipment, manage intelligence data, prepare EW and intelligence reports, extend and mesh intelligence services, conduct preventive maintenance on assigned equipment, execute electromagnetic attack (EA), and assist in the operational control and management of SIGINT/EW/CO personnel, equipment, and facilities. 12. MOS 2691, Signals Intelligence/Electromagnetic Warfare Chief (MGySgt to MSgt) PMOS, DIR INTEL a. Summary. Duties encompass signals intelligence (SIGINT), electromagnetic warfare (EW), planning, personnel and asset management, collection management, analysis, dissemination efforts, and ensuring national-to-tactical SIGINT/EW integration. SIGINT/EW Chiefs also supervise the activities of personnel performing communications intercept, electronic reconnaissance, radio direction finding, analysis and reporting functions, intelligence support to CO, and EW operations. Additionally, they serve in staff billets as operational advisors designated by the commander or cognizant staff officer. b. Prerequisites (1) Must hold MOS 2629. (2) Must be a U.S. citizen. (3) Must successfully complete a counter-intelligence scope polygraph examination. nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
